g.id: STEP 1 - WHAT MAY CARRY A PIPE

g.text: STEP 1 - WHAT MAY CARRY A PIPE

g.id: EXCLUDED - a dual carriageway (cannot be dug up, trunk included), a roundabout, a turning link, or a dead stub. Crossing a dual carriageway is allowed, at right angles only
STEP 2 - WHERE A STREET JOINS THE MAIN PIPE, FORMING THE SUBNETWORKS

g.text: STEP 2 - WHERE A STREET JOINS THE MAIN PIPE, FORMING THE SUBNETWORKS

g.id: Search outward from every point on it at once
Main pipe: western edge, then southern side
Street joins where its route is cheapest
A subnetwork is everything arriving at one point
Plot takes the pipe it FACES
Capped stub-out for when it is built
Spur at right angles, from the plot EDGE
Spacing 100 m to DN315, then 120, 150, 200 m
Bend chamber a few metres short. Turn made in two halves, each under 90 deg
Needs 2 m clear of plots, 3 m of chambers. Flag for a curved-channel chamber
STEP 5 - SIZE AND LEVEL, SOLVED TOGETHER

g.text: STEP 5 - SIZE AND LEVEL, SOLVED TOGETHER

g.id: Smallest size that works, on the TRUE bore
Flow here: properties x 5 people x rate, peaked, plus infiltration
Gradient at least Table 11 and tractive force, at most the 3 m/s cap
Lay the invert downstream, holding 1.30 m cover to the crown
THE 12 m TEST - WHERE A LIFT IS FORCED

g.text: THE 12 m TEST - WHERE A LIFT IS FORCED

g.id: HARD LIMIT, nothing exempt. Pumping station HERE
Rising main sized on PUMP DUTY, not the arriving flow, holding 0.75 to 3.0 m/s
Sewer restarts at normal cover, gravity again from there
STEP 6 - CAN EVERY HOUSE ACTUALLY DRAIN IN?

g.text: STEP 6 - CAN EVERY HOUSE ACTUALLY DRAIN IN?

g.id: Deepen that chamber, then solve the WHOLE network again
Straight back to the 12 m test. This alone added a station on the test area
22 compliance checks. A failure is reported, never exempted
